headline: Solar Farms Become Wildlife Havens With New Certification
meta_description: A new certification scheme is helping UK solar farms protect biodiversity while generating clean energy, with one Essex farm achieving a 65% increase in habita…
summary_short: Wild Power's certification scheme encourages solar developers to create wildlife habitats alongside clean energy. The Dunmow farm in Essex shows what's possible.
body:
As the UK doubles its solar capacity toward 2030, a new certification scheme is transforming solar farms into refuges for wildlife. Wild Power, launched in 2022, assesses how renewable energy developments protect and improve habitats, awarding certification to those meeting strict biodiversity standards. The scheme works like "a fair trade stamp, but for clean energy," according to Wild Power director Joe Arafa—addressing both climate and nature crises simultaneously. So far, just two UK solar farms have earned certification.

The Dunmow solar farm in Essex, a 10MW installation co-owned by Thrive Renewables and TopCashback, became only the second certified site in September 2026. Under the guidance of ecologist Guy Parker, the farm underwent a remarkable transformation: species-rich grassland and wildflower areas were planted, hedgerows restored, and bird and bat boxes installed. The result? A projected 65% increase in habitat biodiversity units and a 19% uplift in hedgerow units—far exceeding the legally required 10% net gain mandated by the Environment Act 2021.

Parker describes the shift from "a pretty bland arable field worked by tractors twice a year" to a thriving ecosystem where butterflies move between yellow agrimony flowers and warblers flit between scrub. He emphasizes that developers should integrate wildlife measures from the planning stage, when costs are minimal compared to the multimillion-pound projects themselves. For solar operators, certification offers tangible benefits: a Wild Power survey found that 50% of renewable energy customers would pay premium rates for wildlife-friendly installations. With the UK's solar capacity expected to reach 45–47GW by 2030, the potential to weave nature recovery throughout the renewable energy landscape is substantial.
quick_facts: Wild Power certification scheme launched in 2022 by UK renewable energy developers
Dunmow solar farm in Essex achieved 65% increase in habitat biodiversity units
UK solar capacity to nearly double from 23.2GW to 45–47GW by 2030
Only two UK solar farms have earned Wild Power certification so far
50% of renewable customers willing to pay premium for wildlife-friendly energy
